title: Energy stored in a capacitor
notes: Charging a capacitor means moving charge from one plate to the other against a rising potential difference. The work done is the energy stored.
At an intermediate charge q the voltage is q/C, so the next bit of charge dq costs (q/C) dq. Integrating from 0 to Q gives U = Q^2 / (2C). With Q = C V this is also (1/2) C V^2 and (1/2) Q V.
The factor one half appears because the voltage starts at zero and ends at V. The average voltage during charging is V/2, and charge Q times that average is (1/2) Q V.

A battery at constant V supplies energy Q V, which is C V^2. The capacitor stores only half of that. The other half is dissipated as heat in the resistance of the connecting wires during the charging current.
The stored energy can be written as a density in the field, (1/2) ε0 E^2 in vacuum. The energy is between the plates, in the field, not inside the metal of the plates.
If an isolated capacitor has its plates pulled apart, Q is fixed, C falls and the stored energy rises. The extra energy is the work you do against the attraction of the plates.

summary: The energy in a capacitor is (1/2) C V^2, which is also Q^2/(2C) and (1/2) Q V. The one half is the average of a voltage that grows from zero to V. The battery supplies twice this energy, and the other half becomes heat. The stored energy resides in the electric field.

mcqs.question: The battery supplies
options: The same energy the capacitor stores

mcqs.question: The energy is located
options: Inside the metal plates as the main store
In the battery after charging is over

exercises.question: A 5.0 μF capacitor is charged to 200 V by a battery. Find the stored energy and the energy supplied by the battery.
steps: The battery supplies Q V = C V^2 = 0.20 J.
The other 0.10 J is dissipated as heat while the capacitor charges.
exercises.answer: 0.10 J stored, 0.20 J supplied by the battery.
